newsitem.title: NIGERIA: NNPC appeals against Nigeria court insurance order.
newsitem.headline: NNPC appeals against Nigeria court insurance order.

text.p: State-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) has appealed against a Nigerian court order that it should insure its assets with state insurer NICON, the semi-official Daily Times newspaper reported on Thursday.

A federal high court judge ruled on Monday that "NICON should insure and re-insure NNPC assets for 1997" and that NNPC and oil minister Dan Etete had no right to transfer the oil company account, worth 2.025 billion naira, to other insurance firms.
In a statement of appeal jointly filed at the higher federal court of appeal, NNPC and Etete said the ruling of the lower court was flawed.
"(Judge Mahmud) Belgore erred in law and went beyond the province of judicial authority in compelling NNPC and Etete to go into an agreement against their wish," it said.
Six Nigerian firms went to court in November to contest who should control the NNPC's lucrative insurance account.
NNPC, 100 percent owned by the federal government, pumps two million barrels of crude oil daily, which accounts for more than 90 percent of Nigeria's foreign exchange earnings.
Its assets include oil refineries, petrochemical plants, oil depots and sundry other properties.
Two of the six feuding firms -- Fidelity Bond of Nigeria and Trinity Mills Insurance Brokers -- said NICON brokered their appointment which entitled them to receive commissions.
National Insurance Corporation of Nigeria (NICON), Nigeria's biggest insurance firm is 100 percent federal government-owned.

Lawyers for Fidelity Bond and Trinity Mills had also wanted the lower court to stop the transfer of the account to the four other firms -- UNIC Insurance, Industrial and General Insurance Company Limited, Inter-Continental Insurance Company Limited and Kapital Insurance Company Nigeria Limited.
The six companies are 100 percent Nigerian-owned.
